The lesson is that the guard told me the right command and I reached for the parts instead.
verification.toolchain: ⚠ A CORRECTION TO THIS SESSION'S OWN EARLIER READING, recorded because it is the kind that looks settled. I checked `command -v soffice`, found it, and concluded the docx/PDF path was viable. It was not: `libreoffice-core` was installed and `libreoffice-writer` was NOT, and build_submission_parts.py's docstring predicts that exact symptom — 'libreoffice-core alone reports every input as unloadable'. Confirmed with `dpkg -l` (no libreoffice-writer, no libswlo in the program dir) rather than inferred from the error. Fixed with `apt-get update && apt-get install -y libreoffice-writer`; the first install attempt 404'd on a stale package index. ⛔ A BINARY ON PATH IS NOT A CAPABILITY.

If those files had been genuinely stale on the trunk a guard would have caught it, so they stay at HEAD. CLAUDE.md §6: a file you have no reason to be committing is the tell.
verification.manifest_ordering: ⛔ SHIPPED IN TWO COMMITS BECAUSE ONE IS NOT AVAILABLE — AUT-PD-138, hit again and handled the way the generator prescribes. Regenerated inside the chain while the tree was dirty, the manifest recorded `git_tree_is_clean_apart_from_this_manifest: false` and --check-archive refused it as a provenance failure. So the content commit lands first, and the manifest is regenerated against the resulting clean tree as this session's LAST commit, where the flag reads true and `git_revision` names a real commit that is actually pushed. ⛔ AND IT HAD TO BE DONE TWICE. The first regeneration named 6a4c833fd correctly; 12 commits then landed and the rebase rewrote that commit, leaving the manifest pointing at a sha resolvable only through this container's reflog while its clean flag still read true and its inventory was still current. Caught by comparing git_revision against `git rev-parse HEAD~1` by hand — nothing required that. Filed as AUT-PD-140.

what_i_got_wrong: Two things, both of the same shape — trusting a cheap signal instead of the authoritative one. (1) `command -v soffice` succeeded, so I told the previous turn the PDF path was viable; the Writer filters were absent and the module's own docstring had already described the failure. (2) I rebuilt with the generators the test names one at a time instead of the canonical chain the same test message points at, and got a partial green that hid three unbuilt PDF variants. ⭐ In both cases the correct information was already written down in the thing that failed. ⛔ AND A THIRD, WHICH REACHED origin/main: I pushed a DUPLICATE LEDGER ID. A concurrent session filed a different AUT-PD-140 and landed first; `ids.next_entry_id` derives max+1 over committed state, so we both allocated it, and the rebase auto-merged both rows with no conflict marker. `priority.py` then refused the entire ledger — the trunk's scorer was broken for the minutes it took to notice. ⭐ THE INSTRUCTIVE PART IS NOT THAT I DID NOT KNOW: the handoff prompt names counting ids after a rebase as one of three measured rules, and I ran that exact check in the same command as the push. The push was not GATED on it, so the guard ran, printed DUPS, and I read the output only afterwards. A check whose result nothing depends on is decoration. Renamed to AUT-PD-141 per priority.py's own instruction — keep the earlier filer's claim on the string, record `_renamed_from`.
